dialogues.text: Wait a moment, we're...

talks.objective: Learn about the situation from Monglane

dialogues.speaker: Monglane
dialogues.text: Your name.

response.speaker: Monglane
response.text: I'm a receptionist here at the Fortress of Meropide. Everyone calls me Monglane. Alright, your turn.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh, Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he}{F#she}'s {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Monglane
response.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon, huh... Never heard of you two. Are you really from around these parts?

response.speaker: Monglane
response.text: Yes, I can see that.

response.speaker: Monglane
response.text: Two names missing... It seems like someone's been slacking off. I'll have to record this. Those who didn't fill the forms in properly will face the relevant consequences...

response.speaker: Monglane
response.text: Anyway, this isn't your fault. No need to worry.

response.speaker: Monglane
response.text: As long as you follow the rules and behave well, you might even have the chance to leave early. You just need to fill the application form and wait patiently for it to be approved.

choices.text: Wait a moment, that's not what I'm talking about...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of that... Did we just complete some sorta procedures? This is going way too fast — Paimon's got no idea what's happening...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's gotta be some kinda misunderstanding...

response.speaker: Monglane
response.text: If you want your case reviewed, please fill the application form in according to this format. That said, the time for that has passed for now, so you'll have to wait for the next application window to open.

response.speaker: Monglane
response.text: If you have any other questions... Ask Darcy. He should be nearby. I'm sure he'll be glad to have a newbie to talk to.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what? This isn't "fine"! Wait, do you already know what's going on? Paimon doesn't get it at all...

choices.text: My great name is unknown to you, huh...

response.speaker: Monglane
response.text: Well, I do know the main culprits involved in major cases... Are you accessories to one of those crimes?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Accessories? What? Th—That's not right! We're good people!

response.speaker: Monglane
response.text: Ah, I see, noted.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It sure doesn't sound like you're "noting" anything...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And you can call Paimon Paimon... *cough* Gah, lowering our voices didn't make us sound more serious at all. In fact, we sound super weird!

talks.objective: Learn about the situation from Monglane

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are we waiting for? Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay, let's go, then.

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: Well? Want to go find Estienne with me now?

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: Hi, Estienne. I've brought two new friends with me.

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Your new friends may have come at a bad time. See that? They're gonna be at it for a while.
...That's an unscientific way of keeping score. Besides, the participants were unsupervised. Is that any way to produce convincing results? I'm calling for a reassessment.
This is a competition, of course we should have a refined system and fair rules. Participants who don't follow the rules should be disqualified.
You talk a good game. I'd expect nothing less from someone who's been through the wringer.

If you're referring to the fraudulent thesis case, I've already made my point several times now. The case is still under investigation. It's useless to try and attack my character with something like that.
If you say so. After all, you're the only one who knows the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: Oh, it's Genevieve and Rave again. I'll talk to you about my thing later then, I'm gonna bounce for now... I'll leave my two new friends to you!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Darcy makes a dash for it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He left us, just like that? Some guide, Paimon gives him zero stars! Zero!

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Mr. Guard, as the organizer, it's not exactly proper for you to stay out of this discussion of the rules, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Haha, this is just a game to pass the time. How was I supposed to know you'd all get so riled up over it... let alone take it this seriously.

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Right, why don't we introduce the rules of the game to the new players?

choices.text: A game? I'm definitely gonna win.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh, there's no game the two of us can't win! Wait a sec, we still don't know what the game even is yet...

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Don't try and change the subject! We're already halfway through the game, and they don't even know the fundamental rules. They can't just join in now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, what are you guys playing?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Coupon Millionaire.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon has never heard of such a game...

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: Of course not, this is just what the heartless guards play to make fun of us. Everyone loses, and I'm sure you know who wins.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: That's not true. You work to earn Coupons during the game, and the one that has the most Coupons will get an even better reward from me.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: So everyone wins, but one person wins more than the rest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A reward better than Coupons? What could it be?

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: In Darcy's words, a chance to be under the sun. Some of our periodic checks need to be performed outside, and I get to decide who gets these jobs.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: It wouldn't be very interesting if I just picked based on my preference.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: So I created Coupon Millionaire, and those who want to go outside are free to sign up. Whoever gets the most Coupons wins the game.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: If you feel that your strength alone will be insufficient, you can find others to group up with. As for how you earn Coupons... I don't care about that.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: As far as games go, the rules are really vague.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: It's part of the strategy. Does the Fontaine Research Institute not have similar "games"?

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: How about you, Darcy's new friends?

choices.text: Sorry, everyone, but I'm going to win.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: It's not impossible to come back from behind, but only those who have the means will be able to do it. As for them... Estienne, maybe you should arrange a special competition for children.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Children's competition...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't know who you are, but you shouldn't underestimate us. We've seen some... things! It's just a game, and we gonna cruise through it!
No, I will definitely be the biggest winner.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh wow, a real child! And a confident one, at all!
That's what Cater said, and he's never lied to me.
What are you all doing here?
You again, Estienne?

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: I didn't break any rules, did I? In fact, I even increased everyone's work efficiency, and that should be to my credit.
You know what I mean. Know your place, Estienne. You're a guard, and you should use your powers to make them obey you.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: I have my way of doing things. And you, Noailles... It's been some time since you arrived here at the Fortress. You should try blending in a little more.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Laziness, apathy... I will restore order here, starting with you. Stop this gathering and go back to what you were doing!

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: I am not as lenient as Estienne. If I'm going to restore order, then punishments are a must. I don't think you want to know what they are.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: ...Are there things that even I don't know?

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: I jest. You don't need to waste any of your time on this game that we play to kill time. The Fortress is huge, and I'm sure there are other things that require your attention.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: I don't need you to remind me.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Noailles leaves.\nGenevieve and Rave return to their respective companions.\nThe girl also slips away without being noticed.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: Finally... Being serious can be a virtue, but being overly serious... is something else.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: Anyway, now that the annoying guy is gone, will you join the game, Darcy's new friends?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What sort of person leaves their friends behind, anyway? We aren't his friends! In fact, Paimon's gonna use his uncool nickname to address him! That "Pretty Face" is a jerk!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Huh? Wait a minute, that nickname doesn't sound all that mean...

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: Haha, alright, then. What should we call you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Call me Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}. As for the game...

choices.text: We'll need more time to think about this.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: Sure. If you change your mind, please feel free to talk to me.

choices.text: I haven't agreed to play yet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, we don't even know what this game is. If it's an eating competition, Paimon will absolutely play! But if it's some sort of game involving a lot of hard work and very little reward... then you can forget about it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Hehe, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Player

dialogues.speaker: Player

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Are you ready to go?

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Ouch!

dialogues.speaker: Clynes
dialogues.text: I'm sorry! Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: It's the evil sorcerer's magic! We'll be trapped if we get caught in it!

dialogues.speaker: Galvaryet
dialogues.text: Sorry, the light's broken, and this expert here isn't anywhere near as good as he claimed...

dialogues.speaker: Clynes
dialogues.text: I never said such a thing.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you! It's alright, you're a good sorceress.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: But that bright light really hurt my eyes...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Sorry for the delay. About the way I said I got the Coupons earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What did you do to him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Someone that aggressive doesn't seem like the type to take advice from anyone. Why would he give up so easily...?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Just a few small tricks.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: "The culprit is where he should be." This is an undeniable fact.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Making someone as straightforward as him "certain" of an undeniable fact isn't exactly hard.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Like that time with Julien?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: That's right. Just like that time with Julien.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I've been here for a long time, as you know. After staying in one place for a long time, it's only natural to pick up a few handy tricks to exert some degree of influence over your environment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Changing a stubborn person's mind with just a few simple phrases almost sounds like magic... Could there have been times when we were also influenced by magic without even knowing it?

choices.text: Considering how pure-hearted you are, Paimon, that is a worrying thought.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You, too, {NICKNAME}! Wait a minute... You're not saying Paimon's as gullible as Julien, are you?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: It's not as simple as it looks — there are always limits to the application of tricks like these, and the results aren't always what you'd hoped for.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: It's like with Julien — He always had a knack for art, but he lacked confidence because of his visual impairment. The "certainty" that he could draw well was inside him to begin with.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: But in other cases, the concept of "certainty" is just too abstract, making it difficult to predict the outcome.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: So, I did take a chance this time. I just thought that if he held us up here, it would keep delaying the plan to get Lanoire out of the Fortress...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Besides, I doubt you wanted to be questioned by him repeatedly either.

choices.text: You shouldn't take chances like that.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: You're absolutely right.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Back to the matter at hand... If you've changed your mind and want to back out, I understand completely. Lanoire might be sad for a time though. For her, playmates like you are hard to come by.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... We've already made a promise to her, so we can't just go back on our word now. Right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Consider this our way of helping her out!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, where is she?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: She went on an adventure early this morning — probably to rehearse for what's to come after she leaves this place. It's just as well, I have a few headaches to go take care of soon...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: You can usually get a reward for helping others — including the guards — take care of some headaches.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, we totally get that. Sounds just like some of the Adventurers' Guild's commissions.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I see. Would you two join me on this next commission, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure! Where are we going?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: The abandoned production zone in the lower levels.

choices.text: This doesn't mean I trust you.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Of course. Knowing that our goals are aligned for the time being is enough.

choices.text: Well, you've got to take chances to achieve your goals.
Would someone even realize that they're being influenced?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Paimon was already a bit sleepy, but now her head is totally spinning...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Phew, guess our adventure's almost at an end. The Coupon Cafeteria's our final stop.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So the ultimate destination of adventuring is a good meal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not bad, right? Adventures take a toll on your body, so eating afterward is a must.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: That's right! And I've never seen someone as small as Ms. Paimon! You're even smaller than Ms. Sigewinne. You should eat more, so you can grow bigger!

choices.text: I think Paimon's fine just the way she is.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks so, too!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: By the way, do the two of you have any Coupons?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Paimon doesn't think so...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, that means we get no food. Oops.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: No, don't worry! Just talk to Bran, and you'll get a yummy free meal!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Bran's the clockwork meka over there. It was broken, but Wolsey repaired it.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: You only get a free meal once per day, though, and you won't know what you'll get. The best thing you can get is the Tasses Ragout.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you won't know what you'll get? Why can't you order what you want?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Wolsey says that it's meant to be both a surprise and a risk precisely 'cause it's a free meal. If you don't want any risks, then you've gotta use Coupons.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Will the two of you try the free meal?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon will give it a try! Paimon is always lucky, and this stuff's free! How can free meals be bad?

choices.text: The thought of Paimon growing up... Ugh, that gives me a headache.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, you're probably thinking about something rude right now, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Caterpillar probably went to get Coupons elsewhere, but he left us some clues...)

choices.text: I think Paimon's fine just the way she is.

choices.text: I'll have a free meal, please.

response.speaker: Bran

response.speaker: Bran
response.text: Enjoy.

response.text: And Paimon, too!

response.speaker: Bran
response.text: Enjoy.

response.text: I'll have one, too.

response.text: Understood. Enjoy.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, let's open our meals together, alright? Three... Two... One!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Wow, mine's Tasses Ragout!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: What did you two get?

choices.text: Is there a pot? I'll cook my own meal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't want to eat anymore.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: So I got the only good meal? Will there be enough if we split it into three portions?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: There's even a fortune inside. What do yours say?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's fortune says, "Luck only brings fleeting pleasure, lifelong happiness requires hard work." ...Grr, now Paimon's mad!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #How about you, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Things happen. Don't take it personally!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just... wow.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Mine says, "Misfortune is an illness, and caring friends are the cure."

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: The two of you went on adventures with me, so you're definitely caring friends... But you got the disgusting meals...

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: The Sorceress said that I must remember to pay it forward. So now it's my turn to cure you!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Let's go to the Rag and Bone Shop.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, this looks kinda disgusting.

response.speaker: Bran
response.text: Negative. According to the "Fortress of Meropide's Coupon Cafeteria Regulations," only one free meal per day shall be permitted per person.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm getting one for Paimon, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, don't forget about Paimon!

response.speaker: Bran
response.text: ...Understood.

response.speaker: Bran
response.text: Enjoy.

choices.text: I'll have five hundred free meals.

response.speaker: Bran
response.text: Negative. According to the "Fortress of Meropide's Coupon Cafeteria Regulations," only one free meal per day shall be permitted per person.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm getting some for everyone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you seriously trying to feed everyone here? We just need two!

response.speaker: Bran
response.text: ...Understood.

response.speaker: Bran
response.text: Enjoy.

talks.objective: Go to the Rag and Bone Shop with Lanoire

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Hello, Alvard!

dialogues.speaker: Alvard
dialogues.text: Hey, Skylark, want a Fonta? We just got a new shipment. How about your friends?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is the Rag and Bone Shop.

dialogues.speaker: Alvard
dialogues.text: If you have Coupons, we have everything from home supplies like Hydro Phantasm Taint-B-Gone...

dialogues.speaker: Alvard
dialogues.text: ...To devices that can help you in the Pankration Ring. Our wares are trusted and loved by all and sundry! You name it, Rag and Bone Shop has it!

choices.text: We'll take some Hydro Phantasm Taint-B-Gone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We don't really need this, do we?

response.speaker: Alvard
response.text: The special items must be pre-ordered, though. Or if you're lucky enough, you might find what you want on the for-sale list.

response.speaker: Alvard
response.text: We do have the other stuff stocked at all times. So, back to my question. How about some Fonta?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Hm, I want everything in Uncle Alvard's store.

response.speaker: Alvard
response.text: That's not going to be a problem. Let's see... We're almost through with this shipment, and only food and drinks are left. But they'll cost you a good number of Coupons.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really!? Are you sure it won't be a problem?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Problem? If you mean Coupons, Cater gave me a ton of them, so I should have enough. The food and drinks here are really great, and you're going to love them, Ms. Paimon!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Cater said that Coupons make unfair things fair. Only I got the delicious Tasses Ragout at the Coupon Cafeteria, and that was unfair.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: So now I'm going to use my Coupons to buy something delicious for the two of you!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Let's dig in!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, that was supposed to be my line, you two!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Estienne said that hunger and gross food reduce our work efficiency and put us in a bad mood.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: We're going to see Cater soon, and we wanna be in a good mood when we see him. That's why we need to fill our stomachs with delicious food.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: We're counting on you, Uncle Alvard.

response.speaker: Alvard
response.text: Sure. Thank you for the business!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If Lanoire says so... We'll dig in!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Yup! Have a good meal, Ms. Paimon!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Feasting with Lanoire...\nEverything that couldn't be finished ends up in Paimon's pack.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew! That was amazing! Paimon's so full, she can barely walk. She's getting sleepy, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why are we here again?

choices.text: If you can't remember, then maybe it wasn't important.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon remembers now! We're supposed to be looking for Cater.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Let's go! But I don't know if he's there. If not, we can wait. He might be back soon.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: That's a strange question! I've always been here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Lanoire said there are plenty of delicious food and drinks...

choices.text: Devices that help you? What do you mean?

response.speaker: Alvard
response.text: They're for regulars only. Or, if you happen to have friends who are our regulars, I suppose I can show them to you...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Cater! I'm back.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Welcome back, Lanoire. Looks like you've made some friends.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #Yes, they're {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Ms. Paimon. Ms. Paimon is small and she can fly, but she's not a bird.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: She's not a Seelie either. Maybe a small Oceanid? No wonder no one has seen anything like her, or knows anything about her!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon's Paimon.

"Cater, what story are you gonna tell me today? I've already heard a lot of stories with heroes as the main characters..."
"Today I'll tell you a story about a little girl, then."
"A little girl... Can a little girl also be the main character?"
"Of course she can. It's her own story, after all. In other stories, she might be a hero herself, or even an evil dragon. There are all kinds of roles she can play."

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Long, long ago, there was a little girl who lived in a giant's garden.\nThe giant took special care of the flowers in the garden, and wouldn't allow anyone to pluck even a single one of them. To keep intruders out, the giant built a towering wall around it.\nBecause of this, the little girl living in the giant's garden had never set foot outside of it even once. The giant always told her that the world outside was a dangerous place, and that the garden was the safest place she could live in.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
"And then what? Did the little girl listen to the giant? I bet she didn't. If she did, then the story would end there!"
"You're right. The little girl never was one for doing what she was told."
"Uh-huh...?"
"As for the rest of the story, well, let's save that for next time."

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: I consulted the records from the last hundred years, and I couldn't find any record of a "Caterpillar." In light of this possible mislaying of documents, we'll need your cooperation to recreate them.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: There's nothing pressing about the matter, if you ask me. What's the rush about?

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Estienne, I often get the impression that you couldn't care less about restoring order to this place.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: I can't agree with your viewpoint. People who habitually indulge their every whim just can't see that too much freedom actually does them harm.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: I'll restore order to this chaos using my own methods. I'll advise you again not to stand in the way of my work.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: "Chaos"? Isn't that just another word for "thinking on your feet"? *sigh* You know what? Forget it.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Is Caterpillar your real name? Additionally, I'll need you to state your crime in as much detail as possible — the time, location, as well as the final sentence pronounced.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: The more details you provide, the greater the likelihood we'll have of retrieving your records. If your file was indeed lost, we can fill in a portion of your records based on your statement.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I've been called Caterpillar for as long as I can remember. I think this name suits me best, and it's the closest thing I have to a real name.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Real name... Caterpillar. Confirmed to be correct. Next, state your crime.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I carried out a certain task under my master's orders. I failed, but some people suffered because of it nonetheless. This was my crime.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Your master? I'll need their full name. Also, when did this occur?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Unlike me, he has many names. This happened a long time ago.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: ...Are you messing with me?

response.speaker: Caterpillar

response.speaker: Black Screen

response.speaker: Black Screen
