dialogues.text:
One day, the little girl heard the sound of a woman's voice coming from beyond the towering wall.
Kind-hearted giant, I am in need of the little purple flowers from your garden. Would you please give me some?
The giant refused, of course, and furiously bellowed at the woman on the other side of the garden wall to leave at once.
But the woman did not leave, and from a short distance away, she lamented that she had journeyed from afar for the little purple flowers in the garden, which she needed to cure a sick friend's illness.
Hearing the woman's plight, the little girl felt sorry for her and her friend. The giant had so many flowers in his garden. Surely having one or two less wouldn't hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Thus, the little girl approached the garden wall and whispered to the woman that she was willing to bring the woman a few of the little purple flowers. Except, the little girl said, the giant wouldn't let her leave, and the garden's walls were so tall that she wasn't sure how she would be able to get the flowers to her from inside.\nFrom the other side of the wall, the woman told the little girl that she was actually a witch that knew many magic spells, and if the little girl could bring her the flowers she needed from the giant's garden, she could use her magic to help the little girl leave that garden...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "Did the little girl decide to help the witch? Hmm... I bet she did. Otherwise, the witch wouldn't be able to cure her friend's illness, right? But... But the giant said she couldn't leave the garden. If she left, wouldn't she get punished somehow?"\n"It's getting late. Let's leave that part of the story for next time."

talks.objective: Meet back at the usual place

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: Having fun playing house with the kids?

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: I believe we've met.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did you need us for something? We're rivals, you know. Did you really come to see if we're having a good time?

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: I have many qualities, and one that has benefited me greatly is my curiosity.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: I always want to get to the bottom of things I don't understand, so I tend to know the facts better than others.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: Looks like we'll enjoy talking to each other then.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: I just wanted to know why you decided to take part in this game.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: If it was for the chance to get out, I have another route that I can show you...

choices.text: I like playing games, and I like winning even more.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: #{M#Remaining vigilant around your enemies is wise, but I'm not necessarily your enemy.}{F#There's no need to be so wary of me, miss. I bear you no ill will.}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean by that?

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: What I mean is, if you only want to win, then why don't we work together?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But aren't you already in first place?

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: That's precisely why we both stand to benefit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Wait a minute, we joined to help Lanoire out...

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: That little girl? In that case, if you're willing to join up with me, I'll grant any wish she has as well.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds too good to be true.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: Then I'll be frank — this is a matter of honor. Caterpillar and I have some... unresolved history.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: I don't know what he said to pull one over on you... but I'm telling you, he's a monster. A monster in human skin.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: What are you all talking about? Not some sort of rule-breaking scheme, I trust?

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: ...Tsk.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: Ah, Mr. Noailles. Your timing couldn't be better. Could I ask you about the results of the investigation into Caterpillar...

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: The majority of his records are missing, but it's fine. The culprit is where he should be, and everything is as it should be...

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: His records are missing? That's impossible. He definitely had a hand in this...

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: ...The missing records need to be recreated. Right. How could I have forgotten about that? Hmm...

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: ...Right, go finish your tasks now. I don't want to see you loitering around here.

choices.text: I have nothing to say to a competitor.
It is pretty fun, to be honest.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: Looks like Estienne really should hold a children's version.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: Just as I thought.

talks.objective: Meet back at the usual place

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon! Welcome back!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: We brought quite the haul back today. Our current standing should be...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dang it! We only just pulled ahead of Darcy...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: That's great! We're not in last place anymore!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But there are four of us...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Yeah, and we're doing great!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But are we really gonna be okay like this? We still have two big hurdles ahead of us...

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: You promised me we'd win for sure, right, Cater?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: That's right. So, don't worry too much, you two. I know that may sound strange, but...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Sometimes forgetting about the outcome and enjoying the fun to be had in the process isn't a bad way to go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, if you say so...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, speaking of that, Caterpillar, we received an invitation from the guy who was in first place earlier. But he was super rude, and he said that... you're a...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Anyway, it wasn't very nice of him!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What happened between you two?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Just a few minor differences of opinion. He invited me to join him as well, but having no real reason to accept, I declined his offer.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Later, he tried to get some of his lackeys to teach me a lesson... It's true, I am a monster — the kind people like him would do well not to provoke.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: D—Don't say that! Surely you didn't end up this way because you wanted to, right, Caterpillar?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: If Cater is a monster, then he's one of the good ones! Just like how there are good sorcerers and bad sorcerers... *yawn*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's the matter? Are you sleepy, Lanoire?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Mm-hmm... But I haven't heard the rest of yesterday's story yet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you're tired, you should go for an early night.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon... Will we still meet again tomorrow?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why are you asking that all of a sudden?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: If... If you don't want to be on the same team as us anymore...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you talking about? Didn't we say we'd get first place together? There are still two more teams ahead of us, so we have to make tomorrow count!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #Yeah, you're right! *yawn* I'm so sleepy. Let's do our best tomorrow... Sweet dreams, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, sweet dreams, Ms. Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's rest.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "Where we last left off, the witch told the little girl that she would use her magic to help her leave the giant's garden if the little girl brought her the little purple flowers she needed."\n"I'm really sleepy, but I want to know what happens next. What did the little girl do? Does the witch cure her friend in the end?"

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Although the giant had warned the little girl of the many dangers of the world beyond the garden wall, the little girl had never seen what the outside world was like, so she didn't know what "danger" even was.\nShe told the voice on the other side of the wall that she would help bring her some of the little purple flowers. So many identical flowers were growing in the garden, and each looked as beautiful as the next. She didn't know why the giant treasured each and every one of them so.\nThe little girl heard laughter from the other side of the wall. Later, with a bouquet of flowers in her hands, the little girl rode a gust of wind over the wall to the world outside.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The tall witch took the little purple flowers from the little girl's hands. The little girl, thinking she had done a good deed, was very pleased with herself. But when she tried to return to the garden, she discovered that the wall, the garden, and the giant were no longer there.\n"Good witch, I'd like to return to the giant's garden now. Could you please use your magic to take me back?" The little girl asked.\n"But what can you give me in exchange now?" The witch replied.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "Huh? Then the little girl couldn't go back? I'm glad the witch could save her friend, but... I don't like this story..."\n"Everyone has stories that they don't like."\n"Then I'll tell you a story next time, Cater... I have to sleep now..."

talks.objective: Meet back at the usual place

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Hello...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's getting deja vu... Did you need us for something?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Alright. I'm hoping you'll join us in launching a protest against Estienne.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Since you're taking part in this game as well, I think you'll understand my position. The rules should be more open and transparent...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's the catch?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: The competition should restart with the new rules in place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? Wouldn't that make all the hard work we've done so far be for nothing?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: What's so crazy about that? It happens all the time in academia — you realize that there's an error in your thesis or methodology, and it completely invalidates the conclusion you arrived at after years of research.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Pretty sure that's nothing like this...

choices.text: Maybe for the next time he runs the game... Just play it as it is this time around.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Indeed. Iterating and improving the rules will take time. We may not be able to get them implemented until the next time the game is held...

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: No, I need this game to be fair. To me, delayed fairness is a pointless loss. I've lost so much time already because of this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Paimon thinks you have the right idea, but... but this isn't a decision that can be made by just us, right? Maybe you could go ask the others as well...

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Estienne will only change the subject, and as for Rave... You kids had better keep your guard up around him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Us kids..."? Hmm, that kinda grinds Paimon's gears, but maybe that really is how other people see us...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, thanks for the tip. But Paimon's not sure we can help you.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Fine. I anticipated as much.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Then I'll leave you to it. Good luck out there. My luck hasn't exactly been great, but I won't be throwing in the towel that easily.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: O—Okay. Paimon also hopes that your luck improves...

talks.objective: Meet back at the usual place

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's that guard doing here...?

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: Just who I was looking for.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Hang on. I'd like you to answer a few questions first.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: As you probably know, the missing records need to be recreated. This isn't necessarily bad news for him, but without those records, he won't be able to leave this place even if he has legally redeemed himself.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: As such, I hope you can answer my questions honestly.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Do you know when Caterpillar arrived in the Fortress of Meropide?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... He just said that he came here a long time ago, so we don't know when exactly...

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Then I don't suppose you know the specifics of his sentence or crime?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, we don't...

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Do you know anything about this "master" he mentioned earlier?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't remember Caterpillar mentioning him before...

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Have either of you observed anything peculiar happen while speaking to him?

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Not so far? Okay then.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: That's enough questions for today. It doesn't seem like you know very much, but if you do notice anything strange, make sure to report it at once. It's for your own good.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Noailles leaves...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like we don't know much about Caterpillar after all... But if he doesn't want to talk about his crime or sentence or anything like that, Paimon thinks we'd better not press him.

choices.text: I'm not really concerned about any of that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, he didn't ask much about our pasts either.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But whatever the case, he's doing a good deed right now, isn't he?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lanoire seems to really trust him as well... So he's probably not a bad guy... at least for now, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You can never go wrong with a little caution.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After you wait patiently for a little while, Caterpillar and Lanoire return.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon! You're both so fast! I got carried away talking to Ms. Galvana.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: She even gave me some candy! She said they're made from a fruit that grows on the trees in a desert oasis...

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: I asked her what kind of place a desert oasis might be, and she said it's a little body of water surrounded by a vast sea of sand.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Doesn't that sound just like the Fortress? Except... Y'know, opposite, since this place is surrounded by water.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Once you leave this place, maybe you'll get to go there and see it for yourself! That reminds me, after all the hard work we've done, we must have advanced by now, right?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Speaking of that, I asked Estienne, and here's where things stand at the moment...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean we basically haven't advanced at all!? How could that be?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Looks like the competition's been hard at work, too.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Indeed. Rave has some contacts, and the researcher and detective's assistant will have their own ways.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Surely this isn't the time to be singing our rivals' praises? Is there really nothing we can do? We're definitely gonna lose at this rate...

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: We're gonna lose? But if we lose, we can all stay here in the Fortress, right?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: We've talked about this before, Lanoire. If we stay here, we'll have to worry each day about being taken away by evil sorcerers.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Oh... then I guess it would be better to leave. But... But Ms. Paimon said we're definitely gonna lose...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—We're not gonna lose! The game's not over yet, there's still enough time. We're gonna win this!

choices.text: If we don't win this time, there's always next time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Don't be such a wet blanket, {NICKNAME}! Have some faith. We can definitely win this time!

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: There isn't much time left until the deadline Estienne set. Let's just meet at the message board in the administrative area next time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh, there isn't much time left until the final results are announced, is there... Paimon has a feeling she's gonna toss and turn in bed tonight...

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: You can tell me in secret if you feel scared, Ms. Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, seriously? A kid like you, worried about Paimon...? Paimon won't get scared! You're the one who should be scared! Paimon hopes you'll have sweet dreams, Lanoire!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Don't worry, I've had lots of nice ones. In fact, I wish I could give some to the two of you!

choices.text: An underdog victory would be more exciting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The fact of the matter is, there are only two teams ahead of us. We've got nothing to worry about!

choices.text: He does seem a little suspicious...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Suspicious, huh... Well, he is kinda mysterious...

choices.text: The stories he tells have a rather hypnotic effect...

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Hypnotic? What stories? What are they about?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—They're just children's fairytales, they're not about anything important.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Well, children like you shouldn't even be here to begin with. If you end up leaving this place, I hope you don't come back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Huh? O—Okay.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: The investigation is ongoing, so I can't disclose any specifics to you. However, I'd like you to answer a few of my questions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's rest for a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "It's my turn to tell a story! I've heard enough stories to tell one of my own now."\n"Alright, you can be the storyteller this time."\n"Okay. My story will also begin in the giant's garden..."

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
Long, long ago, in a garden full of purple flowers, there lived a prince, a princess, and a brave hero... Oh! And the ruler of the garden — a giant with a nasty temper.
What the witch wanted more than anything were some of the purple flowers, but the mean giant treasured them so much that he wouldn't let anyone pick even a single one.
"Kind-hearted Mr. Giant," the witch asked, "I am in need of the little purple flowers from your garden. You have so many already, could you please share just one with me?"
But the mean giant refused. "Every flower in my garden belongs to me," the giant shouted, "I won't share them with anyone!"

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "Kind-hearted Mr. Giant," the witch continued, "please hear my tale. I traveled here from a fountain in a far-off, distant land. An Oceanid there has fallen ill, and the scent of those purple flowers brings her comfort. If you could give me just one of them, perhaps her condition will improve..."\nBut the giant, who didn't have an ounce of compassion in his heart, callously refused the witch's request. What did an Oceanid in a faraway land have to do with him?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "Then," the witch asked, "is there anything I can do for you? I know many magic spells, and I could use my magic to help you with someone in exchange. Will you agree to my request, kind-hearted Mr. Giant?"\nThe giant thought it over, then said that he had lost something very important to him. If the witch could use her magic to help him find it...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "So, they made a deal?"\n"Yep! In the end, the witch's friend recovered and the giant found what he had lost. Isn't that a better story? At least in this story, everyone gets a happy ending..."

talks.objective: Go to the Administrative Area Bulletin Board

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Strange, Caterpillar and Lanoire aren't here yet.

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: Why bother coming when you know you're going to lose?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I wouldn't be so certain of that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! You're only ahead of us by a little...

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: A little? Haha.

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: Can the results be announced now, Estienne? Actually, no... Let's wait a little. After all, the best must be saved for last.

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Looks like we don't have to wait long. Here they come.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}! Ms. Paimon! Have you seen the results yet? Did we win?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We don't know yet...

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: Well, seems everyone's here. Would you announce the results now, Estienne?

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Of course. Oh, but the results on Caterpillar's end still need to be calculated...

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: My, my, what a cruel guard, toying with us from start to finish like that.

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: Why don't you wring out the last bit of mercy in your heart and let them know that the gap between us is too wide to cross? Stop torturing us with false hope.

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: These aren't the final results, but...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: We should be able to win once we add the Coupons that Cater got today, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on, why have Genevieve's team's points been cleared out?

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: I was against it. But this is the more logical approach with respect to the results.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's that supposed to mean...? Whoa, Rave's team has so many points!

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: He doesn't need the chance to leave, and we don't need to place first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean you gave all your Coupons to Rave? Isn't that against the rules?

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: There's no rule forbidding it. I was originally in favor of amending the rules to ensure fair play, but no one else seemed to be in support of that.

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Indeed, there isn't a rule forbidding that. *sigh* This competition would have been far more exciting if everyone could have fully used the rules to their advantage.

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: More exciting for you, maybe. Rules don't mean a thing in a game as boring as this one. At the end of the day, it's a question of upholding one's honor.

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: Alright, now that the scores have been announced, isn't it time for the final results?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Our points from today haven't been added yet.

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: Hmph... A drop in the ocean.

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Now that everything's been added, here's what the results look like.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #Yes! {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, look! Look! We won!

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: What...? That's impossible! What did you do?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... that many? Paimon's lost count... Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It's a trick even simpler than magic.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I used the Coupons I'd saved up in the past to hire a bunch of people to help me work. What we have now is the product of their work this whole time. And I believe this falls within the rules, too.

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Even if it does, that's an insane amount...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I also have my reasons for needing to win, and I'd even gotten help from my two friends. It would be a real shame if we lost now.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Vanity, perhaps.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: #Since everything's been tallied, it's time to announce the final results. The winners of this game are Caterpillar, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, and Ms. Paimon.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: No objections, I take it?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: There's nothing I can say, except that it looks like I picked a fight with the wrong opponent. I ended up in here last time for striking someone in anger. I won't make the same mistake this time.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: ...You'll pay the price for the choices you made.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, Paimon didn't expect to hear someone actually say that.

choices.text: Pretty cliche, if you ask me.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: Is everyone ready? If so, let's set off now.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: Let's do this before Noailles gets back. I hope he can understand that his thinking isn't wrong, but that it's just not suited for a place like this.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: You're ready, aren't you, Lanoire?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Uh-huh! I've already said goodbye to everyone.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We're also ready to get going whenever.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: Alright. Just keep quiet for a while. I've made some arrangements in advance, so we shouldn't run into any problems.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's even more cliche!

choices.text: I think it's time to announce the final results.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You have remained inside the light's detection range for too long. The Fortress of Meropide's guards have detained you for being suspicious.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You are taken to the reception area...

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: How about it? Wanna go look for Estienne together with me?

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: Newcomers? And two of you, to boot? Welcome! Welcome to the Fortress of Meropide! I'm Darcy. Outside, they call me "Pretty Face," but that's just not cool, if you know what I mean!

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: That's what you were thinking too, right? That's why I decided to give myself a new, super cool nickname! I'm called Dirty Face now! What do you think? Pretty sick, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: More importantly, we have some questions...

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Ooh, of course! It's perfectly normal for newcomers to not know what's going on. Dirty Face Darcy, at your service!

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Go ahead, ask me anything!

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Haha, you came here and you don't even know what this place is? Oh, based on how you're dressed, I don't suppose you're Fontainians. Alright, looks like you really could use an introduction.

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: For-tress-of-Me-ro-pi-de. Got it? This is the Fortress of Meropide. Anyone can get into a regular routine and live a carefree life here. Pretty sweet, right?

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: What, you want to hear the tale of "Pretty Face Darcy"? Why don't we go sit in the Coupon Cafeteria for a bit then? It's a long story, after all, so I'll need some time to tell it.

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: I'll treat you to some Fonta... Wait, that's not right. I'll be the one telling the story, so it's you who should be treating me to a Fonta. Although, newcomers won't have any Coupons... In that case, you'll owe me two Fontas.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Why would we owe you a drink for telling your own story, let alone two? We don't want to hear it, then.

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Really? Are you sure? *sigh* That's too bad. Pretty Face might be a lame nickname, but all kinds of stuff happened back when people called me that...

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: But it's fine. If you regret it later and decide you do want to hear my story, I'll move it up in my schedule. You know where to find me, right? Right here!

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Huh? That's what you want to ask me? Wait, I get it, you want me to guess, right? You don't look like evil villains, so you definitely didn't do anything serious...

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Did you steal or damage some precious cultural relics? No, that can't be it. Did you collaborate with some bad actors and disturb the peace? Hmm, maybe not, actually. Something more minor... Ooh, you didn't pull a dine-and-dash, did you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It was Paimon, she ate it all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #*gasp* How could you say that! You clearly ate a lot of it too, {NICKNAME}... But no, we didn't dine and dash!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon has no idea what happened to land us here...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Darcy all about what happened before...

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Oh! Well, in that case, all you can do is apply to have your case re-examined. But, as Ms. Monglane said, the window for that has passed. You'll just have to wait until the next opportunity comes up.

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Also, you'll want to make sure you fill out the form correctly. If you get anything wrong, your application will be flat-out rejected. You may not have known that, being new here and all...

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Don't be fooled by her appearance, she's a real nag about document formatting. There's no room for error with her, not even for the guards.

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Live, work, play — whatever you feel like. Trying to get some sun might be tricky though, haha. That said, it wouldn't be completely impossible, either.

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: If you're interested in getting some sun, I could bring you to see a few people... Oh, I mean real sun, of course, not the searchlights...

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Um... Unless you're actually the type that prefers the searchlights? I'm not one to yuck anyone's yum, but try not to get burned.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't understand any of what you're saying right now... But does getting real sun mean getting out of this place? If that's the case, count us in!

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Missing the sunshine outside already? Alright, I'll take you to see Estienne in a bit. Hmm, I think we can still make it in time? Well, let's go ask him first.

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: I heard Alvard's got his hands on some rare stuff. If you're interested, you could go to his Rag and Bone Shop and ask. Maybe he'll let you take a look.

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Also, that new guard, what's his name... Noailles. I heard he doesn't like Fonta! What a stick in the mud... Not only that, he also wants to shut down the Pankration Ring. Tch.

choices.text: That's all I wanted to ask.

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Alright. If you have any more questions, just come find me. Dirty Face Darcy is at your service!

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: For now, why don't I take you to see Estienne? He's a guard, but he's cool, if you catch my drift!

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: One time in the Pankration Ring, he slipped me a bottle of Pure Water before I got in the ring! I still lost in the end, though...

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Anyway, he's one of the good ones. Whenever there's trouble, he'll take care of it. So? Wanna go see him now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It is a generally recognized title, after all. Just thinking about it fills Paimon with courage.

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: #Hello, {M#sir}{F#ma'am}, and hello to your cute companion! Dirty Face Darcy, at your service!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dirty Face?

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: That's right, just call me Dirty Face Darcy. They used to call me Pretty Face on the outside... but that nickname is just so lame!

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: Please, just call me Dirty Face instead... Oh, that's just a cool nickname, I wash my face every day. You don't have to stand all the way over there...

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Too bad it's not time for Pankration yet... Let me think.

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: How about this, why don't I take you to have some fun? A few folks have locked horns over the chance to go outside. I had no idea those Fontaine Research Institute guys could dish it out like that...

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: I'm guessing they'll be here any minute now... What do you think? Think of it as an opening act before the real Pankration match starts. Wanna check it out?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, where'd you learn to talk like that? Don't tell Paimon... Don't tell Paimon you've picked up some bad habits... No way! Paimon won't allow it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There you are!

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Oh, you again. And your, uh... Are you a bird, little one?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A bird? Paimon doesn't look like a bird...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean melodic chirping!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: That's so strange. You can fly, but you're not a bird. Are you an evil dragon? Or an evil dragonling?

choices.text: The way you eat and your thirst for wealth certainly fit the bill...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No they don't!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Anyway, {M#he}{F#she}'s {NICKNAME}, and Paimon's name is Paimon. What's your name?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #I'm... Lanoire. {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Ms. Paimon, will you please tell me whether the evil sorcerer is still there?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The evil sorcerer?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Yes, with black clothes and a staff that has branches sticking out of it. Cater said that I mustn't get spotted by that sorcerer, or things will get very bad...

choices.text: Where is this wicked spellslinger? My sword is ready!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why are you playing along? Paimon thinks she's talking about who we just saw.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Must've been a guard, right? So, who's this bad, bad sorcerer? Estienne, or Noailles?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Estienne is a good sorcerer! He brought me flowers when he returned last time. They had the same color as my skirt!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Then Cater taught me to put them into books to make pressed flowers. That way, my books would smell nice, too. Is this what they call the fragrance of knowledge?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Noailles, then.

choices.text: Estienne said he was annoying, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't like him, either. It seems he doesn't think very highly of us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, the evil sorcerer's gone now. Still, why's a little kid like you in the Fortress of Meropide?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: I've always been here. Why does everyone ask me that? It's so strange.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Don't you two have your own home, too?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Home is where your family is.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: That's what Cater said, too, which is why I have a home that I don't know about.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How do you call a place that you don't know home?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Wait, I can't? That's a toughie... But I'm sure Cater knows the answer. He knows lots of things, and a lot of stories!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Might Cater, by any chance, be a kid who looks about the same age as you?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #Nope, he's a lot taller than me, taller than {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, and taller than the evil sorcerer.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: But I think he's afraid of the evil sorcerer. He lost his sword, and the evil sorcerer has a powerful staff, so he hides when the evil sorcerer comes out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (This Cater sounds... mysterious. And maybe Lanoire is just too young? She hasn't been very clear about herself at all. Maybe this Cater knows more?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I guess we can go meet him.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We want to meet Cater. Will you take us to see him?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Sure, but... it's too soon to go back! I want to explore this place while the evil sorcerer isn't here. Will you come with me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just what kind of story are you looking for, anyway?

choices.text: Was it the person that we just saw?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, Paimon thinks so too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why did you hesitate?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm feeling a little tired. Should we rest now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Should we rest now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Should we rest now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Should we rest now?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Sorry for the delay. About the way I said I got the Coupons earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What did you do to him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Someone that aggressive doesn't seem like the type to take advice from anyone. Why would he give up so easily...?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Just a few small tricks.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: "The culprit is where he should be." This is an undeniable fact.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Making someone as straightforward as him "certain" of an undeniable fact isn't exactly hard.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The purer a person is, the more easily they tend to be influenced by others' words.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I've been here for a long time, as you know. After staying in one place for a long time, it's only natural to pick up a few handy tricks to exert some degree of influence over your environment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Changing a stubborn person's mind with just a few simple phrases almost sounds like magic... Could there have been times when we were also influenced by magic without even knowing it?

choices.text: Considering how pure-hearted you are, Paimon, that is a worrying thought.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You too, {NICKNAME}! Wait a minute... You're not saying Paimon's gullible, are you?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: It's not as simple as it looks — there are always limits to the application of tricks like these, and the results aren't always what you'd hoped for.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Once, there was an overly-trusting kid who wanted to progress in the arts. He always had a knack for it, but he lacked confidence because of his visual impairment.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: The "certainty" that he could draw well was inside him to begin with. That's why I didn't turn him away when he came to me for help. Things didn't go quite as I expected in the end, of course, but...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I did take a chance this time. I just thought that if he held us up here, it would keep delaying the plan to get Lanoire out of the Fortress.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Besides, I doubt you wanted to be questioned by him repeatedly either.

choices.text: You shouldn't take chances like that.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: You're absolutely right.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Back to the matter at hand... If you've changed your mind and want to back out, I understand completely. Lanoire might be sad for a time though. For her, playmates like you are hard to come by.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... We've already made a promise to her, so we can't just go back on our word now. Right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Consider this our way of helping her out!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, where is she?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: She went on an adventure early this morning — probably to rehearse for what's to come after she leaves this place. It's just as well, I have a few headaches to go take care of soon...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: You can usually get a reward for helping others — including the guards — take care of some headaches.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, we totally get that. Sounds just like some of the Adventurers' Guild's commissions.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I see. Would you two join me on this next commission, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure! Where are we going?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: The abandoned production zone in the lower levels.

choices.text: This doesn't mean I trust you.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Of course. Knowing that our goals are aligned for the time being is enough.

choices.text: Well, you've got to take chances to achieve your goals.
Would someone even realize that they're being influenced?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Paimon was already a bit sleepy, but now her head is totally spinning...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The north side of the production zone's lower levels.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Maybe we'll even be able to get some Coupons...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The south side of the dormitory block.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Maybe we'll even be able to get some Coupons...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The southeast side of the production zone's upper level.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Maybe we'll even be able to get some Coupons...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Looks like Caterpillar left us a few Coupon breadcrumbs to follow...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll take our chances.

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: Dirty Face Darcy, at your service!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: At whose service? And when? You ran off and left us behind back there!

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: I had to. Once that researcher starts talking, there's no end to it! It was fun the first time, but I've seen it too many times already.

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: That was your first time, right? Was it fun?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon didn't get the point, either.

response.speaker: Darcy
response.text: Too bad the time for Pankration hasn't arrived yet. I think that's more fun! Anyway, we'll just have to wait.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Are you serious, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Come find me if you change your mind. We're already midway through the game though, so joining now means getting a late start. Still, that would make the game more interesting, wouldn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: I told you it's a waste of time to talk to them about these things. They just don't care.

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: You know we're not that kind of people. I can't reach conclusions intuitively like you. I have to do it before making a decision.

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: Did you need me for something?

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: The smiling ones are the ones you've really got to watch out for.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: ...You kids oughta head home. If you still have a home to go back to, that is.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: #{M#You're not going to try to get that woman to listen to reason, are you?}{F#You seem to have more sense than her.}

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: I've got nothing to say about him.

dialogues.speaker: Henaff
dialogues.text: Got any Coupons, boss?

response.speaker: Henaff
response.text: You're not the boss? Why didn't you say so?

response.speaker: Henaff
response.text: You don't? Then I called you "boss" for nothing. What a waste.

dialogues.speaker: Alvard
dialogues.text: Welcome to the Rag and Bone Shop! We have everything... Oops, we don't have anything right now.

response.speaker: Alvard
response.text: We'll get a new shipment soon. Don't forget to come back!

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, and I tried a really wonderful-tasting Fonta... Ms. Paimon drank a whole lot of it, but she didn't drop down at all!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: She must know a lot of powerful magic, then.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Yeah... Ms. Paimon's so strong!

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: I was chatting with Ms. Monglane... She said that Natlan's nothing like Fontaine, and that she really wants to take a dip in a volcanic hot spring.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: A volcano... Is that a flaming mountain? And mountains are... suuuuper tall mounds of rock and dirt, right? Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: You'll get to see all these things for yourself after you leave this place, whether it's volcanos, or anything else.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #Then let's explore those places together, Cater! Hmm... Let's invite {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Ms. Paimon, too. They'll definitely like that!

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: *yawn* I'm so sleepy...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: In that case, go get some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Okay... But I haven't heard the rest of the story yet. I'll rest after I hear the ending...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: The candy Ms. Galvana gave me... is so sweet.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Remember to brush your teeth before bed.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Okay... I will!

dialogues.speaker: Nizami
dialogues.text: Tired from playing with those kids? You can spar with me after you've rested!

choices.text: I'm pretty strong, just to let you know.

response.speaker: Nizami
response.text: The stronger the opponent, the better!

choices.text: Why do you want to spar with me?

response.speaker: Nizami
response.text: Huh? How does the saying go again... "There's no substitute for the real thing"! Sparing with an actual person always beats punching dummies, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Galvaryet
dialogues.text: Will it take this long? You...

dialogues.speaker: Clynes
dialogues.text: I want to be free of these bothersome affairs, too! Really, can you just... please use the devices according to the instructions?

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: Did you need me for something?

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: #{M#Indeed, we only get the occasional bit of rainfall each year.}{F#You're a funny one, miss.}

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: Have a nice day, then.

dialogues.speaker: Henaff
dialogues.text: Hey, do you think there will still be any pay-off in joining now?

dialogues.speaker: Henaff
dialogues.text: This Fonta's too strong. There are quite a few flavors, though...

dialogues.speaker: Henaff
dialogues.text: I think the health drink that guy from Sumeru is working on has some promise. Maybe I should invest a little in it...

dialogues.speaker: Delassaux
dialogues.text: I may not be your friend, but I'd advise against that.

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: ...Sorry, I have some things I need to think about.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: What, you lost your cat, too?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What cat?

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Oh, you don't know yet? Never mind.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: I don't think anyone here loses cats.

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Phew, this is tough work.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: Haha, you guys, too.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: Mental labor is still labor, isn't it? But the scary thing is that, as an imperceptible form of labor, there's no way to determine its value.

dialogues.speaker: Henaff
dialogues.text: After careful consideration, I've decided to invest in him.

dialogues.speaker: Henaff
dialogues.text: Lasting health is more important than a fleeting moment of pleasure or mental renewal, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Henaff
dialogues.text: Everyone's smart enough to understand this, I'm sure.

dialogues.speaker: Henaff
dialogues.text: I think this idea is going places!

dialogues.speaker: Delassaux
dialogues.text: I'd advise you against asking for my opinion next time.

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: ...There's no way we need that many technicians.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Oh, nothing. I was just lamenting how many familiar faces from the Fontaine Research Institute are here.

dialogues.speaker: Rave
dialogues.text: You shouldn't have turned down my offer.

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: I hope you'll be able to stick to your convictions until the end then.

choices.text: Is it too late to back out, then?

response.speaker: Rave
response.text: Opportunities like that only come around once. That's something you should understand.

dialogues.speaker: Henaff
dialogues.text: ...We'll need additional investment to expand production.

dialogues.speaker: Henaff
dialogues.text: It's just that Mora's been a bit tight lately. Do you think you could...

dialogues.speaker: Delassaux
dialogues.text: Nope, don't look at me. I've got nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Henaff
dialogues.text: Don't say that! We're in this together. How about this? When we make a profit, I'll double your share.

dialogues.speaker: Henaff
dialogues.text: ...Still no? Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Delassaux
dialogues.text: I said I've got nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Guess I only have myself to rely on in the end.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Humans are lonely creatures, don't you think?

choices.text: Why this, all of a sudden?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: I tried to rely on others, and it didn't work out.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: I suppose that's to be expected. Good thing I always have a Plan B, so I'm not completely out of options.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can't keep up... Let me think.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're going too fast, let us think about this a little...

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: Oh, sorry! I didn't mean to make you come with me. Take your time, and come find me when you make a decision!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's talk about this later.

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: Just think of it as killing time. Anyway, come find me when you make a decision, and I'll take you to meet Estienne, my guard partner!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's something else I want to ask about.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let me think about it first.

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: Sure thing!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then let's get going.

dialogues.speaker: Darcy
dialogues.text: Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I need a little more time.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's wait a little bit.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Hmm... Then... Then I'll wait for you two here! Don't worry, I'm very patient!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Hehe, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Fourmon
dialogues.text: "Ah! Why you... You she-devil! I remember now, I remember..."

dialogues.speaker: Meilhat
dialogues.text: No no! You must face the audience when delivering the line, with 30% regret, 60% disgust, and 40% appreciation for having survived a catastrophe by sheer dumb luck.

dialogues.speaker: Fourmon
dialogues.text: You should try adding up those percentages and seeing just what the total is...

dialogues.speaker: Meilhat
dialogues.text: Don't mind that, just face the... Right, that chair is where the audience should be. You must look in that direction when saying the line...

dialogues.speaker: Meilhat
dialogues.text: You have to imagine someone sitting over there!

dialogues.speaker: Fourmon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Fine, I'll try again.
